batchName: Late Republic: Caesar in Gaul (58-50 BCE) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Late Republic: Caesar in Gaul (58-50 BCE)

questions.question: Which two barriers did Caesar become the first Roman commander to cross with an army?
options: The Rhine and the English Channel
The Danube and the Black Sea
questions.explanation: Needing headlines, Caesar chose to do what no Roman army had done before. He bridged the Rhine in ten days and later landed in Britain.
questions.sourceQuote: He chose to do what no Roman army had done before: cross both the Rhine and the English Channel.

questions.question: How did Caesar decide to deal with the 80,000 Gallic warriors inside Alesia?
questions.explanation: Caesar chose a blockade over an assault. Vercingetorix responded by sending riders out by night to summon a relief army.
questions.sourceQuote: Caesar chose to starve them out rather than storm the walls.

questions.question: Why did the Helvetii set off from the Swiss plateau in 58 BC?
options: Rome had ordered them to resettle
A plague had swept through their villages
Their harvests had failed for years
They were being squeezed by Germanic peoples
questions.explanation: Pressure from Germanic peoples pushed the Helvetii to migrate westward with their families and herds on 28 March 58 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: The Helvetii, a group of related tribes on the Swiss plateau, were being squeezed by Germanic peoples.

questions.question: What made several Belgic tribes surrender in 57 BC without even fighting?
options: A Roman fleet on their rivers
The sight of Roman siege works
The death of their high king
questions.explanation: Siege works were unknown in Gaul, and just seeing them was enough to make several tribes give up. The main Belgic army had already broken up for lack of food.
questions.sourceQuote: The mere sight of Roman siege works, unknown in Gaul, made several tribes surrender without a fight.

questions.question: How long was Caesar's unusual term as governor when he took over his provinces in 58 BC?
questions.explanation: Governors normally served one year, but Caesar got five, long enough to fight a real war. His provinces were northern Italy, Illyricum and Transalpine Gaul.
questions.sourceQuote: His term ran for an unusual five years instead of one.

questions.question: During Caesar's first landing in Britain, who got the hesitant soldiers off the ships?
options: Crassus's son at the head of the cavalry
A centurion of the Seventh Legion
The standard bearer of the Tenth Legion
questions.explanation: The Tenth Legion's standard bearer leapt into the sea, and the men followed rather than lose their standard. Rome later voted Caesar a 20-day thanksgiving.
questions.sourceQuote: Then the standard bearer (*signifer*) of the Tenth Legion leapt into the sea, and the soldiers followed rather than lose their standard.

questions.question: Who were the Veneti, who defied Caesar in 56 BC?
options: Horse breeders of the Swiss plateau
questions.explanation: The Veneti were seafaring tribes of Brittany whose sturdy oak sailing ships ruled the Atlantic. They seized Roman officers sent to collect grain.
questions.sourceQuote: In 56 BC the Veneti, seafaring tribes of Brittany, seized Roman officers sent to collect grain.

questions.question: In 49 BC Caesar crossed which river, marking Italy's border, to start a civil war?
questions.explanation: Crossing the Rubicon launched the civil war, which Caesar won. In 44 BC he was named dictator for life.
questions.sourceQuote: In 49 BC he crossed the Rubicon, the river marking Italy's border, and won the civil war that followed.

questions.question: Ambiorix, who led the winter revolt of 54 BC, was the leader of which tribe?
questions.explanation: Ambiorix led the Eburones, a tribe of north-eastern Gaul. His trickery led to the destruction of about a legion and a half.
questions.sourceQuote: Ambiorix, the shrewd leader of the Eburones, a tribe of north-eastern Gaul, saw his chance.

questions.question: What did the Helvetii do to their villages before setting off on their migration?
questions.explanation: They burned their villages so there could be no turning back. Caesar refused them passage through his province and attacked them anyway.
questions.sourceQuote: They burned their villages so there could be no turning back.
